title: Round 18 Four Corners state-frame USGS GNIS source register
scope: All-GNIS starter registers for Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico, completing the Four Corners state set beside the round-16 Arizona frame. Every seeded row reproduces one accepted USGS GNIS Geocoder candidate; South Platte River also carries a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check.

usgsGeocoder.use: Fuzzy candidate discovery only. A candidate was accepted only when Name, Type, State, County, GnisId, Latitude, and Longitude all matched the intended feature. Political divisions and same-name records of another class or county were rejected explicitly where relevant.

gnisDomesticNames.use: Per-ID identity checks for South Platte River (201759) and the three Eddy County Pecos River candidates (900170, 900171, 900172). The South Platte check confirms Class=Stream and coordinate sequence 1; the Pecos checks do not identify one statewide river record.

selectionRules: VERIFIED=1 is claimed only for an exact official name, compatible GNIS feature class/type, intended state and returned primary county, permanent FEATURE_ID, and an official point returned by a cited USGS service.

Grouped Geocoder Types map explicitly to stored row classes: Cities & Populated Places to Populated Place, Lakes & Reservoirs to Lake or Reservoir according to the official feature name and kind, and Streams & Canals to Stream for the accepted river records.
A stored GNIS primary point is never described as a municipal boundary, street-address geocode, generic centroid, shoreline polygon, summit/valley/flat outline, or river centerline.

If exact-name candidates remain indistinguishable, or the state-filtered screen returns no intended feature record, the feature is omitted from the gazetteer and may appear only as a generalized context corridor.
Statewide frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized corridors; no bundled DEM or surveyed boundary is implied.

identityDecisions.candidate: Green River, Utah: Stream 1428399, populated place 1428398, Division 1939372
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The stream primary point does not verify the town or political division.

identityDecisions.reason: The states=UT screen returned same-name Lakes & Reservoirs records in Duchesne, Garfield, Rich, and Summit counties, including two distinct Rich County FEATURE_IDs (1438482 and 377174); no per-ID statewide-lake identity was established in this round.

identityDecisions.candidate: Grand Lake, Colorado: Lake 204950 and populated place 202505
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The lake primary point is not the town point, boundary, or shoreline.

identityDecisions.decision: Seeded after a GNIS Domestic Names per-ID check confirmed Class=Stream, the 439-mile tributary description, and coordinate sequence 1 at the stored point.
identityDecisions.serviceDiscrepancy: Both the Geocoder County field and Domestic Names Primary County field say Logan County while coordinate sequence 1 is a headwaters-area point from the Deckers map. The stored county preserves that returned primary-county provenance and is not asserted as the county containing sequence 1.

identityDecisions.candidate: Arkansas River and Rio Grande under states=CO; Rio Grande, San Juan River, and Canadian River under states=NM
identityDecisions.decision: No gazetteer rows seeded; generalized context corridors only where shown.
identityDecisions.reason: The state-filtered Geocoder screens did not return the intended exact stream records (Arkansas River Canyon and Rio Grande canals/places are different features; San Juan River and Canadian River returned empty arrays under states=NM).

identityDecisions.decision: Omitted from the Utah and Colorado gazetteer rows; generalized Colorado context corridor only.
identityDecisions.reason: The returned GNIS primary point (31.9, -114.9508333) lies outside both frames, as already recorded for California, Nevada, and Arizona.

identityDecisions.candidate: Sierra Blanca Peak, Summit 920702, versus Sierra Blanca, Mountain Ranges 912567
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded Sierra Blanca Peak as the Summit row.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The summit primary point is not a mountain-range polygon.

identityDecisions.candidate: Animas River: San Juan County Stream 900284 and Hidalgo County Stream 900283
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the San Juan County record for the northwestern New Mexico river.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: It does not verify the separate bootheel stream of the same name.

identityDecisions.candidate: Pecos River, Eddy County FEATURE_IDs 900170, 900171, and 900172
identityDecisions.decision: Omitted from the gazetteer; generalized context corridor only.
identityDecisions.reason: GNIS Domestic Names identifies 900170 as Class Canal and both 900171 and 900172 as Class Stream, each with only nearby Lake McMillan-area coordinate sequences. Neither Stream record is distinguished as the statewide Pecos River record, so choosing one would violate the identity-safe rule.

identityDecisions.candidate: White Sands and Carlsbad Caverns, New Mexico
identityDecisions.reason: The White Sands screen returned a populated place, census place, missile-range records, and a broad Area record without establishing a dunefield-specific identity-safe class for this starter batch; the exact Carlsbad Caverns Geocoder screen returned an empty array.

identityDecisions.candidate: Wheeler Peak in New Mexico (928839) and Nevada (861956)
identityDecisions.decision: Seeded the Taos County record in New Mexico and retained the White Pine County record in Nevada.
identityDecisions.notClaimed: The same official name does not make the two state high-point records interchangeable.

knownLimitations: Utah, Colorado, and New Mexico are starter registers, not statewide GNIS extracts. Each contains 12 deliberately selected identity-safe rows.
The USGS Geocoder is a suggestion service; exact-match screening and, for South Platte River, a Domestic Names per-ID check are part of the evidence.
GNIS point data do not supply the displayed terrain. All three frames use explicitly synthetic relief gaussians and generalized context corridors.
State frames are rectangles, not state-boundary clipping masks. Utah and New Mexico rectangles include small areas outside their notched state outlines; no boundary geometry is claimed.
